## Core Legislative Pillars

### A. The "Proof of Need" Mandate
- Any digital entity soliciting crowdsourced funding exceeding $1,000 within a 30‑day period must provide verifiable, third‑party documentation of necessity.
- For medical or veterinary crises, this requires a redacted, official invoice or statement from a licensed professional prior to activating public donation links.

### B. Truth in Streaming / UTPCPL Integration
- Aligns with Pennsylvania’s Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law (UTPCPL).
- Streamers are legally bound to “Truth in Advertising” standards regarding their physical living conditions, location, and operational status.
- Presenting a fabricated lifestyle or deceptive crisis environment to secure direct financial aid (e.g., CashApp, PayPal) constitutes Theft by Deception.

### C. Financial Transparency & Daily License Fees
- Establishes regulatory boundaries for non‑charitable crowdfunding.
- Tracks the velocity of unverified public donations to prevent interstate wire fraud and consumer exploitation.
